examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: For unspanned records, blocking factor is floor(block bytes/record bytes). Sparse primary indexes typically store one anchor per ordered data block; dense indexes cover every search-key value. Binary search over an index costs logarithm of its block count, and accessing the data block may or may not be included in the requested cost.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
There are 12000 fixed 100-byte records in 1024-byte unspanned data blocks. A sparse index uses 20-byte entries. How many index blocks are required?

**Answer: 24.** Each data block holds 10 records, so 1200 blocks need 1200 anchors. Each index block holds floor(1024/20)=51 entries. Required blocks=ceil(1200/51)=24.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Scan efficiency differs from point-lookup efficiency. Unclustered index traversal may fetch a different data page for many consecutive records.

A hash index is suited to equality search, not generally ordered range traversal.
